page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-4 is an instance type belonging to the Network Optimized server family. The machine provides 4 dedicated virtual CPUs running on the x86_64 architecture and is configured with 31.0 GB of total system memory. This resource distribution yields approximately 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU core, catering to configurations requiring higher memory density per compute unit.

Hardware accelerators are absent from this server, with a GPU count of zero. The instance does not include bundled local disk storage, meaning persistent storage requirements must be handled using network-attached block devices. Additionally, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned directly by default.

From an infrastructure and cost efficiency perspective, c4n-highmem-4 provides dedicated core allocation paired with high memory capacity without the overhead of specialized hardware accelerators or attached local NVMe media. This setup is effective for workloads with distinct RAM demands that do not require high local IOPS.
Recommended workload profiles include in-memory databases, caching tiers such as Redis or Memcached, data processing pipelines, ETL tasks, and memory-intensive microservice architectures.
